# $crav1-update-kit

lane: cross-cutting | group: Start | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.131.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Update the installed kit on the current branch to a published release.
use_when: The installed kit should move to a published release, or an early-access flag should be listed or changed
reads: Reads `plugin.json` or the `Kit version:` line, the published `vX.Y.Z` tags, the old release, the new release, `vendors.json`, `.crav1/kit.json` when it exists, `.crav1/flags.local.json` when it exists, and the working tree. It does not read a branch or an open pull request as a target.
writes: Writes kit-owned files on the current branch after a yes, including the Codex tree under `.agents/skills/` when Codex is selected, writes `.crav1/kit.json`, writes `.crav1/flags.local.json` and `.crav1/.gitignore` for `flags-on` and `flags-off`, replaces a copied template that still matches the old release apart from line endings, and commits `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB` when the user chose the commit. `add codex` commits `Add CRAV1 kit vendor codex vX.Y.Z`. `remove codex` commits `Remove CRAV1 kit vendor codex vX.Y.Z`. A migration listed for the jump is dry-run and written only on its own yes, and is left unstaged. When `kit2` is on, the update installs kit 2.0 at user level from the newest published `v2.0.0-*` pre-release, and from the bundled tree when that lookup or fetch fails.
leaves alone: Leaves specs, `walk-progress.md`, `build-progress/`, plans, tasks, notes, playbooks, the build map, persist rules (except a stale commit-style rule, 1.176.0), the transfer data policy, `kit-maintainer.mdc`, the project's `.gitignore`, and the project's `AGENTS.md` alone. A skill folder that does not start with `crav1-` stays a project file. A `crav1-2-` skill or agent, `.crav1-2/`, and `sot/` stay. Copilot is not installed by this release. Does not switch branches, rebase, or push. A plugin install gets no kit commit. With no flag file, kit 2.0 is not mentioned.
limits: a target that is not a published release tag stops in one line. A clash is not overwritten. An edited template is listed and left. The kit source checkout is refused. An agent's yes does not write, commit, or push.
flow:
- when `kit2` is on, plan and apply install kit 2.0 from the newest published `v2.0.0-*` pre-release.
- The fetch uses the same short temp folder, `core.longpaths=true`, `core.autocrlf=false`, and clean check as `fetch`.
- A failed lookup or fetch uses the bundled tree and `kit2_line` says a newer 2.0 may exist.
- `kit2_line` names the version that will be installed and the version installed now.
- When that engine already matches and `repo_writes` is 0, `card` is null and the ending says the repo kit is current and kit 2.0 is current, with nothing to do and no reload line.
- The plan `files` object carries counts and the changed lists.
- The unchanged list is omitted unless `--list-unchanged`.
- Never pipe or redirect plan or apply output.
- Pass apply `ending_args` to `update_kit.py ending --vendor codex`.
- A user-level kit 2.0 install with no repo files changed says `Kit 2.0 installed in your user folder; reload to load its skills.` The plan `card` omits commit options when `repo_writes` is 0.
- That card is `install-kit2` or `stop`.
- A null card means the repo has nothing to commit.
- early-access flags live in `.crav1/flags.local.json` for one repo.
- `.crav1/.gitignore` lists `flags.local.json`.
- The project `.gitignore` is not changed.
- Words are `flags-list`, `flags-on <flag>`, and `flags-off <flag>`, and one command may name several flags.
- `kit2` (experimental) installs kit 2.0 at user level from the same release through `v2/install.py` when it is on.
- When it is off and kit 2.0 is installed, the update offers `uninstall-kit2` or `keep-kit2`.
- The kit 2.0 result is one line.
- With no flag file, nothing about kit 2.0 is printed.
- Pass `--old` and `--new` (or `--new` on add, `--old` on remove).
- A `crav1-` name pattern is not the list.
- A skill or agent named `crav1-2-`, a `.crav1-2/` folder, and `sot/` are not written, staged, or deleted.
- With no version, the target is the latest published 1.x tag.
- `v2.0.0` and `v2.0.0-alpha.1` are not offered.
- `.crav1/kit.json` lists the vendors.
- `add codex` copies `vendors/codex/` into `.agents/skills/` and does not upgrade the other vendors.
- `remove codex` deletes kit-owned files that still match the release; a local edit is a clash (`keep` or `take`); other files stay.
- `detect` adds `vendors_from`.
- The project `AGENTS.md` is never written.
- `vendors.json` lists each host: the folders the kit owns, the frontmatter a skill needs, the command prefix, and extra files.
- Cursor and Claude Code reproduce the 1.200 allow-list.
- `detect` reports `vendors`.
- `vendors --root .` lists each folder and skill count and writes nothing.
- `--vendor codex` prints `$crav1-` on a Run next script; the default prefix stays `/`.
- a stale commit-style rule is written, removed and committed by the kit itself instead of being refused as a project file; a stale rule whose asset is gone from the new release is listed under `delete`.
- The run ends `Run next: nothing needed now.`, never a `Next:` line.
- a persisted commit-style rule that is the old release's copy, or names the missing `crav1-draft-commit-message/` skill, is rewritten from the current message-only asset in the same yes.
- A rule changed by hand is left and listed in `style_rules_left`.
- **`$crav1-update-kit`** takes an optional `to vX.Y.Z`.
- With no version, the target is the latest published 1.x release tag.
- A 2.0 tag is not offered.
- `main`, a branch, a commit, and an open pull request are refused in one line.
- It detects the installed version from `plugin.json` or the `Kit version:` line in `crav1-docs/reference/workflow.md` (the changelog heading when that line is missing).
- Before any write it shows which branch that is, that only this branch gets the new kit, and that other branches stay on the old kit until this branch is merged into them (merge develop into the branch; never rebase).
- A copied `docs/specs/_template/` or `docs/system/_template/` file is replaced only when it still matches the old release apart from line endings.
- The commit message is `Update CRAV1 kit vA to vB`.
- The heads-up card is not skipped by a word in the opening message.
- In Windows PowerShell 5.1, `curl` is an alias for `Invoke-WebRequest`.
- On Windows, use `python` or `py`.
- `fetch` clones with `core.autocrlf=false`.
- `fetch` clones into a short temp folder by default with `core.longpaths=true` and `core.autocrlf=false`, and refuses an incomplete checkout (git status not clean) before any plan.
- The `ending` move tells the user to reload the window after an update and names `$crav1-design-architecture resume <topic>` for open design topics.
called_by: Called by the user, or by a guild agent. The user's yes in this run is still required before a write, a commit, or a push.
runs by itself: Calls no skill. Runs `scripts/update_kit.py --vendor codex`.
you run next: nothing needed now
first: `$crav1-update-kit Update the kit in this consumer project.`
walkthrough: from-update-kit.md
